central_unknown: Whether Ferrari's recent upgrade momentum carries to Mexico City's unique high-altitude, low-downforce circuit, and whether Red Bull or Mercedes emerges as the stronger second constructor alongside Ferrari.

budget_tiers.fills: Hulkenberg, Lawson or Lindblad, Bearman/Stroll as price floor filler

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 28.8 exp pts, proj 38.8, ppm 1.6, MEDIUM risk, predicted P1→P1. Highest expected points of any driver this weekend. FanAmp had Verstappen as a top-2 lock in Austin and rated him similarly for the triple-header stretch. DNF probability 0.12 is manageable. 90% CI [-9.6, 51.0] shows significant upside.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: ML projects 28.4 exp pts, proj 35.1, ppm 1.19, LOW risk, DNF 0.04 — lowest DNF probability among top drivers. Predicted P3→P2. FanAmp consistently rated Antonelli as a must-have and potential 2x candidate. BoxBox ML shows him essentially tied with Verstappen on expected points but with far lower risk. Safer captain floor.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: ML projects 24.9 exp pts, ppm 1.76 (highest among top drivers), value 1.02, MEDIUM risk. Predicted P2→P3. Ferrari's upgrades have been trending well per FanAmp's paddock reports, and Leclerc himself said one big upgrade package can move you from P4 to P1 constructor. Best value among premium drivers at 24.4M. Lower ownership as captain = differential edge.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Six consecutive 0.6M price rises per F1FantasyPolePosition. 81% chance of price increase per F1 Fantasy Tools. Essential budget builder. ML data for Audi shows constructor exp 15.0 pts — modest but Hulkenberg is the primary contributor.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: F1FantasyPolePosition favors Lawson over Lindblad long-term due to 3-race moving average after Singapore's big result. 82% chance of max price increase. Racing Bulls ML constructor exp 26.3 pts, LOW risk. Strong budget tier anchor.

buy.name: Oliver Bearman
buy.note: 82% chance of price increase per F1 Fantasy Tools. Only needs -2 pts for max price rise. Good overtaking form from Singapore. Cheap filler that actively builds budget.

consider.name: Arvid Lindblad
consider.note: No grid penalty this week (unlike Austin). Racing Bulls are strong mid-tier. 59% chance of max price increase. Slightly less favored than Lawson long-term per F1FantasyPolePosition but still a solid pick.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: High-risk, high-reward differential. FanAmp flagged him as interesting when starting from the back with overtake potential. May lose ~0.6M in value. Only for budgets above 140M that can absorb the price drop.

consider.name: Isack Hadjar
consider.note: ML projects 8.7 exp pts, ppm 0.93, MEDIUM risk. FanAmp noted Hadjar said the car looked 'horrendous' in Austin FP2 — concerning if trend continues. Viable if running Red Bull constructor but carries uncertainty.

avoid: Alex Albon — Williams struggled badly in Austin, never completed a representative flying lap due to track limits. FanAmp explicitly said to avoid Williams.
Franco Colapinto — DNF'd sprint and GP at Singapore, needs 39 pts just to avoid price drop. Never on fantasy radar per FanAmp.
Fernando Alonso — F1FantasyPolePosition gives only 60% chance of price increase, risky asset. Aston Martin underperformed at Singapore despite favorable circuit characteristics.
Carlos Sainz — ML data from BoxBox showed him predicted P18 with -1.5 pts in recent analysis. Poor value.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: F1FantasyPolePosition noted this is part of a triple-header stretch with 6 races remaining. If your team needs significant restructuring to accommodate the Verstappen/Antonelli/Leclerc core plus budget builders, a wildcard here saves transfer penalties. Otherwise save for a sprint weekend where lineup flexibility matters more.

chips.name: 3x Boost
chips.reason: BoxBox activated 3x boost over limitless in Monza because it scored higher in simulations. Mexico's non-sprint format with clear top-2 captains (VER/ANT) makes it attractive. However, saving for a sprint weekend where 3x applies across both races may yield more total points.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: BoxBox showed limitless scored ~8 fewer points than 3x boost in their Monza simulations. Best saved for a sprint weekend or a round where your budget severely constrains your optimal lineup.

chips.name: 4A (No Negatives)
chips.reason: Best deployed at high-chaos tracks or sprint weekends where DNF risk is elevated across multiple drivers. Mexico's predicted DNF rates are moderate (VER 0.12, ANT 0.04, LEC 0.13).

watch_items: Ferrari upgrade performance: Leclerc topped both FP1 and FP2 in Austin — watch if that pace translates to Mexico's high altitude. ML projects Ferrari constructor at 59.2 exp pts, close behind Mercedes (60.1).

McLaren upgrade integration: Norris said big packages 'take time and patience.' ML projects Norris at only 15.8 exp pts (MEDIUM risk, DNF 0.17) — significantly below top-3. Monitor if McLaren finds pace in practice.
Isack Hadjar car confidence: Described the Red Bull as 'horrendous' in Austin FP2. If he continues to struggle, Red Bull constructor becomes less attractive vs Mercedes despite similar pricing.
Turn 1 chaos potential: Lawson described T1 incidents as 'a lottery.' Mexico City's tight first sector could produce similar lap-1 carnage, benefiting backmarkers with overtake potential.

Mercedes constructor vs Red Bull constructor: ML has Mercedes (60.1 exp) slightly ahead of Red Bull (49.8 exp) but Red Bull's projected points (61.3) are close due to Verstappen's upside. Key decision point.
George Russell tire strategy and quali pace: Ran mediums through most of Austin FP2, masking true pace. ML projects only 16.1 exp pts — well below Antonelli's 28.4. Monitor if Russell closes the gap.
arc: Mexico City is the second race of a triple-header that includes Austin, Mexico, and São Paulo. With six races remaining in the F1 Fantasy season, this stretch is critical for budget building and chip deployment. Hulkenberg's six consecutive price rises make him a near-mandatory hold through this block. The Ferrari upgrade trajectory from Austin should crystallize in Mexico — if their pace is genuine, Ferrari becomes a lock constructor through São Paulo and potentially Las Vegas. The Lawson vs Lindblad decision also has multi-race implications: Lawson's Singapore result inflates his 3-race average, making him the better value hold through the triple-header. Teams should position themselves now for São Paulo's likely sprint weekend, where chips like 3x boost or limitless could yield maximum value. Red Bull vs Mercedes as the second constructor will be the key strategic fork for the remainder of the season.
